HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Household Objects — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the soft furniture of belonging: the clock, the picture frame, the vase, the cushion and the curtain — the things nobody needs but every home keeps.

What is this?

Household objects are the small keepers of a home&rsquo;s feeling: a clock to tick, a frame to hold a face, a vase to hold flowers, a cushion to hold a head, a curtain to hold the day out.

What does it mean?

These words carry feelings with them — the frame holds someone loved, the vase holds something grown. Vocabulary tied to affection is the vocabulary children keep.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and a slow walk through your own home, visiting the real versions. Each one gets its word and one sentence about what it holds or does.

Why this matters

This is the lesson where the child learns that homes are decorated on purpose — someone chose the frame, someone picked the flowers. Next comes "can we pick the flowers?"

What it teaches

Affective vocabulary (holds, keeps, loves), noticing detail (what is IN the frame?), and the cushion-curtain pair that appears in every soft room.

Words to learn

clockpicture framevasecushioncurtainhousehold

Say this to your child

“"Household objects — the keepers! The clock keeps the time, the frame keeps a face, the vase keeps the flowers, the cushion keeps your head, the curtain keeps the night."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "five things that make our house ours — let us visit them."
  2. The clock: hold a finger to your ear-watching, tick, tick — what is it saying?
  3. The frame: who is in it? Say the name — the frame holds people we love.
  4. The vase: are there flowers today? Whose room has one?
  5. Cushion and curtain to finish: one to lean on, one to close the day — both words said twice.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Household Objects" sit over a round clock, a standing picture frame, a blue-striped vase, a soft square cushion and blue curtains with tied-back ties.

Ask your child

"What does the clock do all day?" (tick — keep the time) "Who is inside our picture frame?" "What holds flowers?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might appoint the clock the house&rsquo;s heartbeat, choose which picture earns the frame spot next, or arrange every cushion into a throne before sitting.

Out in the real world

Frames and vases appear at every grandparent&rsquo;s house — and now the child can greet them by name and ask whose face that is. The words make visiting richer.

Try it together

Cushion Corner: build a reading corner with every cushion in the house, sit inside it, and name the household objects you can see from there. The softest vocabulary lesson available.

Understanding check

Ask: "What keeps the time?" (the clock) "What holds someone we love?" (the picture frame) "What closes the day at bedtime?" (the curtain)

This lesson pairs with the Household Objects flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
